name: Hepatic Porphyria

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Acute Hepatic Porphyria

criteria.description: Elevated urinary porphobilinogen during acute attacks
Presence of recurrent neurovisceral attacks with abdominal pain
Identification of pathogenic mutations in HMBS, PPOX, or CPOX genes
Exclusion of other causes of abdominal pain and neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated urinary porphobilinogen during acute attacks plus recurrent neurovisceral symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autonomic neuropathy with tachycardia and hypertension
searchTerms: nerve damage causing fast heartbeat and high blood pressure
autonomic nerve problems with tachycardia and hypertension
autonomic nervous system disorder with rapid pulse and elevated BP
motor nerve impairment in arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Psychiatric disturbances including anxiety and depression
searchTerms: mental health issues like anxiety and depression
psychiatric symptoms including nervousness and low mood
emotional disturbances such as anxiety and sadness

occasional.symptomName: Dark or reddish urine during attacks
searchTerms: dark or red urine during episodes

rare.notes: More common in variegate porphyria subtype
searchTerms: skin sensitivity to sunlight with blisters

laboratory: Increased urinary porphobilinogen and delta-aminolevulinic acid during attacks
Elevated liver enzymes in some cases
imaging: MRI may show reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome (RPLS) in severe cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in HMBS gene (acute intermittent porphyria)
Pathogenic variants in PPOX gene (variegate porphyria)
Pathogenic variants in CPOX gene (hereditary coproporphyria)
other: Darkening of urine upon standing due to porphyrin oxidation

distinguishingFeatures: Fever and localized right upper quadrant tenderness
Absence of neurovisceral symptoms and porphyrinuria
Progressive symmetrical weakness without abdominal pain
No porphyrin precursor elevation typical of hepatic porphyria

redFlags: Rapidly progressive motor neuropathy leading to respiratory failure
Severe hyponatremia causing seizures or altered mental status
Recurrent unexplained severe abdominal pain with neuropsychiatric symptoms
references: Anderson KE, et al. Recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of the acute porphyrias. Ann Intern Med. 2005.
Balwani M, Desnick RJ. The porphyrias: advances in diagnosis and treatment. Blood. 2012.
Pischik E, Kauppinen R. Neurological manifestations of acute intermittent porphyria. Cell Mol Biol (Noisy-le-grand). 2009.
